Source library · drug development

Public FDA records with IND information

Study the decisions behind human testing: earlier IND reviews, later development discussions, and marketing-review letters that reveal what FDA asked for.

34 verified records · 24 review-package entries + 10 complete-response-letter entries

Start with the stage

An initial IND may build on earlier human experience. Later toxicity studies, trial changes, and marketing requirements answer different questions.

Check the record type

An original review, a later summary, and a letter are different windows into development. None is automatically the complete IND application.

Read status in context

A complete response letter declines a marketing application in its current form. It is not an IND rejection. Some letters concern products later approved.

How far did the search reach?

Complete bounded screen: CRL text snapshot

All 458 records in the openFDA snapshot were screened for IND-related terms. The dataset was updated 13 August 2026. Of 26 keyword matches, 10 were retained after passage review and PDF verification. The others were routing language, OCR errors, or references too limited for this reading list.

This was a keyword screen followed by manual triage, not a manual reading of every page of all 458 letters. A source can be missed when the relevant words are absent or OCR is poor.

Targeted search: approval-review packages

Six previously verified programs were expanded with 18 additional packages. Search terms targeted original IND reviews, earlier-review appendices, clinical holds, study requirements, dose decisions, and FDA correspondence.

The Drugs@FDA download contains 7,857 Review-type index entries in this snapshot. These have not all been read for IND content. The library therefore does not claim to contain every public IND-related record.

Sources: FDA CRL database ↗ · CRL API ↗ · Drugs@FDA downloadable data ↗

The Approved/Unapproved labels on CRL entries describe the FDA dataset snapshot, not a live worldwide status check. A product can have other approved formulations, uses, or applications. Public disclosure and package dates do not necessarily date the underlying studies.

Read the date, the stage, and the limits

Page references use the PDF viewer’s one-based file pages, including cover sheets. They may differ from the printed page numbers. If a viewer ignores a page link, enter the listed number manually. Multiple listed pages are selected reading locations, not a claim that the entire intervening document was reviewed.

IND information is generally confidential. Public approval packages and newer CRL disclosures can reveal selected material, while protected information remains withheld. Absence from this library does not mean a public record does not exist; absence from a public document does not mean a study was not done. 21 CFR 312.130 ↗ · 21 CFR 314.430 ↗
